page.title: Telemetry
page.description: Export each step an actor takes as an OpenTelemetry span, with its logs and metrics, as OTLP bytes your code sends to a collector.

hero.headline: See what your actors did in OpenTelemetry
hero.lede: Each step an actor takes becomes a span with its event and the states it left and entered, in the caller's trace when it passes one. Your code sends the OTLP bytes to the collector it chooses.

section.heading: Decide where the OTLP bytes go
section.p: The host writes OTLP requests, the protobuf bytes a collector takes at /v1/traces, /v1/logs and /v1/metrics. Your code posts them where it chooses, and retries when it must (operating a host).
A step's span holds the event, the transitions, and the states left and entered. Each <log> and failed action becomes a log record, and the host's counters become metrics.
Turning telemetry on changes nothing an actor does. runs a traced payment in your browser and shows its spans.

section.heading: Export spans to your collector
section.p: A telemetry map in the config makes the host write OTLP. A telemetry handler in the options gets each request it writes as a Buffer, with its signal, 'traces' or 'logs'.
This order continues a caller's trace, and its spans come back with the caller's span as their parent:

example.code: requests before the flush interval: 0 signals: logs, traces spans in the caller's trace: scxml.destroyed, scxml.finished, scxml.macrostep pay, scxml.microstep pay the step's parent is the caller's span: true

section.p: The handler runs in the host's turn, so start the post there and return without waiting for the collector. decodeTraces reads an export without a host (Wire format).
A handler's error is the turn's (Errors). The request it failed to send is not offered again, so retrying is the exporter's job.

section.heading: Choose how soon records are sent
section.p: Every key of the config's telemetry map is optional, and flushInterval decides how soon a request is ready:

row.cell: a request is ready this long after its first record, in the host's clock ticks (system.ticksPerSecond); 0 means only when the staging is full, or at close
attributes on every request, such as service.name (at most 32, text to text)
<log> lines and failed actions as log records
event data and assigned values in the spans; they may hold personal data, so turn this on knowingly
an actor's step is a root span linked to its cause, instead of its child

section.p: The host's clock runs at system.ticksPerSecond, a billion by default, so a flushInterval of 5000 is five microseconds. Most programs that export set ticksPerSecond: 1000 and give the interval in milliseconds.

section.heading: Step a test's clock past the flush
section.p: Once records wait to be sent, the flush is one of the host's deadlines. host.nextDeadline reads it even when no actor has a delayed send left.
The host arms its timer for it, which keeps the process alive until then. A test that asserts no timer is left steps its clock past the flush first:

example.code: the job ended; nextDeadline 1000 traces at 1000 logs at 1000 flushed; nextDeadline undefined

section.heading: Read metrics on your own schedule
section.p: host.metrics() returns the metrics request for the host's counters now, a Buffer for /v1/metrics. On a host without telemetry in its config it throws TA_ERROR_STATE.

section.heading: Close the host to send the last spans
section.p: At host.close() every open span ends, marked incomplete, and the handler gets the last requests before the host is freed.
await host[Symbol.asyncDispose]() also awaits a promise the handler returns there. A host the garbage collector frees without close() sends none of it: close the hosts whose telemetry you want.

section.heading: Continue a trace across requests
section.p: An input continues the trace a W3C traceparent header's text names, and text that does not parse starts a new trace. Pass it as an option:
A send's traceparent is the sending step's context: put it in the header of your request for that send. This handler reads the trace its request would carry:
send.answer() continues the send's trace unless given another, and null starts a new one.
Tracing is on by default (system.tracing), with or without telemetry in the config, so trace context flows when nothing is exported.

section.heading: Seed trace IDs to repeat a test's traces
section.p: A trace the host starts takes its ID from a generator seeded by system.traceSeed. With none in the config, the package draws a random seed for each new host (crypto.getRandomValues).
So two processes, or one process and its restart, do not collide at the collector. The same seed gives the same IDs, which reproduces a test's traces:

example.code: no seed, twice: false seed 7, twice: true

section.p: A host made with Host.restore keeps the snapshot's generators, so its IDs go on from where the snapshot left them.

section.heading: Change what is traced while the host runs
section.p: Call these methods on the host to change what it records while it runs ():

item.text: sets what every actor traces: detail ('summary', 'decisions', 'full' or 'off'), values, sample (the share of new traces sampled, 0 to 1) and rules. It replaces the previous configuration.
adds rules in front of the configured ones for a while (900 seconds by default) and answers { id }. A watch is how an operator looks closely at one chart or one actor without tracing everything.
ends every open span now, as close() does.
reads the spans of a traces request back through the host. decodeTraces(bytes) needs no host, and also gives each span's flags, links, resource and scope.

section.p: A rule picks the steps it applies to, then says how to trace them:

item.text: chart, actor (a trailing * makes it a prefix), event (SCXML's prefix rule), session or from, which is 'host', 'actor', 'timer', 'spawn' and so on.
sample ('keep', 'sample', 'drop' or a share) and detail, at most perSecond with a burst.

section.p: This host samples 1 trace in 100 in summary, then traces every checkout in full for a minute:

example.code: 1 trace in 100, summarized watch 1: every checkout in full for a minute
